phase: Phase 14 — Life 5 Silt Thief combat-policy repair (bounded in-combat tactical reconsideration)
designAuthority: Bounded repair design approved by the owner in the immediately preceding task (verdict D2 — policy + encounter-local Walker memory, implemented as a new additive sibling module, no edit to policy.ts).
repairSummary: Life 5 died fleeing an ordinary enemy 20 times in a row because policy.ts's contextual-combat branch re-derives 'should I flee?' fresh every round with no memory of prior rounds' outcomes, while a real, RNG-free, lower-risk alternative (tactical retreat) sat unused the entire encounter. This repair adds a small, encounter-local EncounterTacticalMemory and a decideInCombat() wrapper (test-utils/canonical/tacticalReconsideration.ts, new) that calls the UNMODIFIED policy.ts decide() first and only substitutes its answer when the chosen survival-movement tactic (flee/retreat/advance) has made no observable progress for REPEATED_FAILURE_THRESHOLD (2) consecutive attempts THIS encounter and a different, not-yet-futile, currently-legal alternative exists. lifeOrchestrator.ts (already the Phase 13 reusable driver seam) gained one new export, resolveCombatEncounter(), wiring the wrapper into combatLoop.ts's resolveCombatRounds() exactly the way a future Life 6 driver would use it — combatLoop.ts itself is imported unmodified.

thresholdRuling.meaning: A tactic becomes reconsiderable only after it has produced 'no-progress' TWICE in a row within the current encounter (i.e., reconsideration is possible starting on its 3rd consecutive selection). A single failure never triggers reconsideration.
thresholdRuling.sourcePrecedent: policy.ts's own Guardian retry branch ('2a', LifeMemory.attempts) already reconsiders after exactly ONE prior failure with no material capability change — but that operates at whole-engagement granularity (a costly, deliberate commitment). An in-round tactic (one flee roll, one retreat step) is cheap by comparison and is not itself evidence of a bad tactic on a single failure. The owner's own design-task semantics ('FIRST FAILURE does not by itself prove a tactic is bad' / 'REPEATED FAILURE means the tactic has now failed again without material progress') read literally as exactly two observations before reconsideration is eligible. Not derived from Life 5's own 20-failure count, and not tuned to any specific enemy.
